subject: Computer Science
instructions:
Report: Quicksort versus mergesort.
Cover the following:
- Average and worst-case time complexity of both algorithms
- Space complexity of both algorithms
- Whether each algorithm is stable
- A benchmark table with at least three input sizes
- A recommendation for sorting a large list of customer records
draft:
Both algorithms run in O(n log n) time on average. Mergesort stays O(n log n) in the worst case, while quicksort degrades to O(n^2) when the pivots are chosen badly, for example on already-sorted input with a first-element pivot.
We timed both in Python on a list of one million random integers: quicksort took 1.9 seconds and mergesort took 2.4 seconds.
For a large list of customer records we recommend mergesort, because its worst case is predictable.
